questions.stem:
The number of isomeric tetraenes (NOT containing sp-hybridized carbon atoms) that can be formed from the following reaction sequence is ________.
3-(but-2-yn-1-yl)cyclohex-1-ene —1. Na, liquid NH₃ 2. Br₂ (excess) 3. alc. KOH→
questions.solution: Na/liquid NH₃ reduces only the alkyne, to the trans alkene ring–CH₂–CH=CH–CH₃. Excess Br₂ then adds to both C=C bonds, giving a tetrabromide (two Br on the ring, two on the chain). Removing four HBr without creating an alkyne or allene forces one pattern: in the ring, C=C forms toward the ring CH₂ and toward the substituted carbon (a ring 1,3-diene), and in the chain the ring-CH₂ and the CH₃ lose H, giving –CH=CH–CH=CH₂. The result is a single conjugated tetraene constitution; the only stereogenic unit is the disubstituted chain C=C next to the ring, which can be E or Z. So there are 2 isomers.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
The number of -CH₂- (methylene) groups in the product formed from the following reaction sequence is ________.
oct-4-ene —1. O₃, Zn/H₂O 2. KMnO₄ 3. NaOH, electrolysis 4. Cr₂O₃, 770 K, 20 atm→
questions.solution: Ozonolysis of the symmetrical oct-4-ene gives two molecules of butanal, and KMnO₄ oxidises them to butanoic acid. Kolbe electrolysis of sodium butanoate couples two propyl radicals to n-hexane. Cr₂O₃ at 770 K and 20 atm aromatises n-hexane to benzene, which has no CH₂ groups, so the answer is 0.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem: The total number of chiral molecules formed from one molecule of P on complete ozonolysis (O₃, Zn/H₂O) is ________.
questions.solution: Cutting all six C=C bonds gives two CH₃CHO from the chain ends plus five fragments, one for each carbinol carbon C(OH)(CH₃). Three carbinol carbons sit between two methyl-substituted alkene carbons, so they become CH₃CO–C(OH)(CH₃)–COCH₃, which has two identical acetyl groups and is achiral. The other two sit between a methyl-substituted and an unsubstituted (CH=) alkene carbon, so they become CH₃CO–C(OH)(CH₃)–CHO with four different groups, which is chiral. So 2 chiral molecules form.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
Considering the following reaction sequence, the correct statement(s) is(are)
Benzene —succinic anhydride, AlCl₃→ P —Zn/Hg, HCl→ Q —SOCl₂→ R —AlCl₃→ S —Zn/Hg, HCl→ a hydrocarbon

options.text: Compounds P and Q are carboxylic acids.
Compounds P and S react with hydroxylamine to give the corresponding oximes.
Compound R reacts with dialkylcadmium to give the corresponding tertiary alcohol.

questions.solution: Friedel–Crafts acylation with succinic anhydride gives 4-oxo-4-phenylbutanoic acid (P), and Clemmensen reduction gives 4-phenylbutanoic acid (Q), so both are acids and (A) is true. SOCl₂ gives the acid chloride R, and intramolecular acylation gives α-tetralone (S); a final Clemmensen gives tetralin. S has no non-aromatic C=C, so it does not decolourise bromine water (B false). The ketones P and S form oximes with NH₂OH (C true). An acid chloride and R₂Cd give a ketone, not a tertiary alcohol (D false).

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem: Among the following, the correct statement(s) about polymers is(are)

options.text: The polymerization of chloroprene gives natural rubber.
Teflon is prepared from tetrafluoroethene by heating it with persulphate catalyst at high pressures.
Ethene at 350-570 K temperature and 1000-2000 atm pressure in the presence of a peroxide initiator yields high density polythene.

questions.solution: Chloroprene polymerises to neoprene, a synthetic rubber; natural rubber is cis-polyisoprene, so (A) is false. Teflon is made by heating tetrafluoroethene with a persulphate (free-radical) catalyst at high pressure, so (B) is true. PVC softens on heating and can be remoulded, so it is a thermoplastic and (C) is true. Free-radical polymerisation at 350–570 K and 1000–2000 atm with a peroxide gives branched low-density polythene; HDPE needs a Ziegler–Natta catalyst at low pressure, so (D) is false.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem: Treatment of D-glucose with aqueous NaOH results in a mixture of monosaccharides, which are
questions.solution: Dilute base removes the α-H at C-2 of D-glucose and forms an enediol (Lobry de Bruyn–van Ekenstein rearrangement). Reprotonation at C-2 from either face gives back D-glucose or its C-2 epimer D-mannose, and tautomerisation toward C-2 gives the ketose D-fructose; C-3 to C-5 are untouched. Option (C) shows exactly D-glucose, D-fructose and D-mannose. The other options include sugars that differ at C-3 or C-4 (galactose, talose, altrose), which cannot form.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper
